body:
Source: the ADLC principle-fidelity audit (docs/reviews/delta.md, seam 1) and a 2026-09-20 repository audit. Re-verified on main @ b2b5c6ea: `gh api repos/voodootikigod/adlc/rules/branches/main` returns one `required_status_checks` rule whose `parameters.required_status_checks` is `[{"context":"test (18)"},{"context":"test (20)"},{"context":"test (22)"}]`, and one `pull_request` rule with `require_code_owner_review:false`, `required_approving_review_count:0`. The jobs `rails-guard`, `mutation-gate` (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and `gate` (.github/workflows/cross-model-gate.yml, workflow name `cross-model-gate`) exit 2 correctly and block nothing: PRs #983, #968 and #907 merged with `rails-guard` red. The repository owner has decided these three become required status checks. The owner changes the GitHub ruleset by hand; nothing in this ticket may call a GitHub write endpoint.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER.
- The status-check CONTEXT GitHub reports is the job id (plus the matrix value): `test (18)`, `test (20)`, `test (22)`, `rails-guard`, `mutation-gate`, `gate`. There is no context called `cross-model-gate`; that is the workflow name of the `gate` job. All are emitted by the GitHub Actions app, integration id 15368.
- The rules endpoint returns an ARRAY of rule objects `{type, parameters}` and only rules from ACTIVE rulesets. It is NOT the legacy branch-protection shape: there is no `required_status_checks.contexts`. Several rulesets can contribute, so take the UNION over every element with `type === "required_status_checks"` of `parameters.required_status_checks[].context`. The endpoint is readable anonymously on this public repository, so any token can read it. For a branch that does not exist it answers `[]` with exit 0, so an empty array must never read as a pass.
- `docs/github-rulesets/main-branch-ruleset.json` is the committed copy of the `main protection` ruleset. `docs/github-rulesets/apply.sh` PUTs it to the ruleset of the same name and docs/RELEASING.md tells the maintainer to run that script. Today it lists only the three `test` contexts, so after an admin adds the gates a later `apply.sh` run would silently remove them again. Its `rules` array has the same `{type, parameters}` shape as the rules endpoint, so the same evaluation function can check it.
- Five workflows have a pull-request trigger: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `cross-model-gate.yml` (`pull_request_target`), `actionlint.yml`, `router-drift.yml`, `ticket-store-platform.yml`. The rest run on push, schedule or dispatch only.
- `scripts/test/*.test.mjs` is one glob segment in scripts/run-tests.mjs (`scripts`), so a new test file needs no registry edit and runs inside the required `test (18|20|22)` jobs. It must pass on Node 18: no `import.meta.dirname` (use `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`), read JSON with `readFileSync` + `JSON.parse` rather than an import attribute. It must not touch the network and must not mint temp directories (scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs fails on an unpaired fixture dir). Inject the `gh` runner instead of shimming a fake binary.
- scripts/mutation-gate.mjs maps `scripts/gate-liveness.mjs` to `scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs` by basename; keep both names exactly so the change stays on the fast mutation path. The mutation gate mutates every changed line of the script, so every decision in it, including the default `gh` runner and the direct-invocation guard, must be reachable from a test or a surviving mutant fails AC17.
- No YAML parser is a declared dependency (`yaml` resolves only transitively) and root package.json is a frozen trust root, so read workflows with a small line parser in the TEST file: inside the top-level `jobs:` block a job id is a key at exactly two spaces of indent (skip `  #` comment lines); inside the top-level `on:` block a trigger is a key at exactly two spaces of indent.
- Model for a push+schedule workflow: .github/workflows/ceremony-drift.yml (pinned action SHAs, `ref: main`, `persist-credentials: false`). Do not add a job to that file; scripts/test/ceremony-drift-workflow.test.mjs pins it.
- packages/prosecute/test/cross-model-gate-workflow.test.mjs (frozen by this ticket) locates steps by the FIRST occurrence of a literal anywhere in cross-model-gate.yml. The header comment you reword precedes every step, so the new wording must not contain any of: `mirror-attestations`, `git -C ./_attestations push origin`, `tier-check`, `actions/checkout`, `run: npm ci`, `persist-credentials: false`, `AUTHORIZATION: basic`, `continue-on-error: true`, `truncation is tracked follow-up`.
- `node scripts/check-reviewer-directed-comments.mjs` is a step of the `rails-guard` CI job. It treats a run of consecutive comment lines as one block, and lines 3-23 of router-drift.yml are one block. It exits 2 when a touched block (or, in a `.md` file, a touched paragraph) both refers to the review process (`round <n>`, `finding #<n>`, `review status`, `review found`, `reviewer concluded`) and carries a word such as `acceptable`, `invalid`, `harmless`, `benign`, `dismissed` or `out of scope`. Line 21 of router-drift.yml carries a parenthetical that begins `(premortem` and cites a numbered item; it must go (item 7). Write every new comment and docs/ci/required-gates.md in plain factual terms with none of those review-process phrases; say `pull-request approval` rather than `review status`.
- Frozen for this change, and the reason the file list is what it is: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `CODEOWNERS`, `scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs`, `scripts/preflight.mjs` and root `package.json` are immutable trust roots of the rail-freeze gate (scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs REPO_TRUST_ROOTS, packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/trust-roots.mjs). Editing any of them makes `node scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs origin/main` exit 2 with no way to authorize it in a single-maintainer repository. Do not touch them. `packages/gate-manifest/**` and `packages/prosecute/**` are enforcement packages (packages/prosecute/lib/tier.mjs); this change has no reason to touch them either. Do not edit `docs/github-rulesets/apply.sh`, the other two ruleset JSON files, or `docs/README.md` (its CI-templates section is pinned by two tests and these files are not templates).
- Another in-flight change deletes lines 9-15 of router-drift.yml (the paragraph naming `check-consolidation.mjs`). If a rebase conflicts in that file, keep that paragraph absent and keep this ticket's wording for line 5 and for the banner.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. `docs/ci/required-gates.json` is the single committed declaration. Shape: `{ "branch": "main", "pullRequestReview": "none", "workflows": { "<workflow path>": { "<job id>": { "blocking": true, "contexts": ["..."] } | { "blocking": false, "why": "<one line>" } } } }`. It names EVERY workflow under `.github/workflows/` whose `on:` block has a `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` key, in this key order: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/cross-model-gate.yml`, `.github/workflows/actionlint.yml`, `.github/workflows/router-drift.yml`, `.github/workflows/ticket-store-platform.yml`, and classifies EVERY job in each. Blocking: `test` (contexts `test (18)`, `test (20)`, `test (22)`), `rails-guard`, `mutation-gate`, `gate`. Not blocking, each with its `why`: `opencode-live-latest` and `codex-live-latest` (advisory drift canaries, continue-on-error), `pre-ga-gate` (all three ADR 0003 items it greps for are checked, so it cannot fail; slated for removal), `actionlint` (workflow lint, advisory), `router-drift` (the same drift assertion already runs inside the required `test` job via scripts/test/router-drift.test.mjs), `ticket-store-platform` (cross-OS matrix for one package, advisory).
2. `scripts/gate-liveness.mjs` imports `node:` builtins only. `main()` runs only when the file is invoked directly, using the `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href === import.meta.url` idiom from scripts/preflight.mjs. Exports, used by every code path: `declaredContexts(gates)` (blocking contexts in file order; throws on an invalid document), `requiredContexts(rules)`, `evaluate({ gates, rules })` returning `{ ok, missing, undeclared, review: { mode, ok, observed } }`, `defaultRunGh(args, { spawn })` (runs `gh` with the given args through the injected `spawn`, default `spawnSync`, `encoding: 'utf8'`, `timeout: 30000`, and maps a spawn error, a signal or timeout, and a non-zero status each to `{ ok: false, reason }`), and `main(argv, { runGh, readGates, stdout, stderr })` returning the exit code. CLI: `--repo <owner/name>` (default: the literal `{owner}/{repo}` placeholders, which `gh` resolves from the checkout; an explicit value must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$`), `--branch <name>` (default: the `branch` field; must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$`), `--json`, `--contexts` (print `declaredContexts` as one JSON array via `JSON.stringify` and exit 0 with no `gh` call), `--help`. Unknown flags and invalid values exit 1. The one and only `gh` invocation is `gh api repos/<repo>/rules/branches/<branch>?per_page=100`: no `-X`, `--method`, `-f`, `-F` or `--input` argument, ever.
3. Exit codes. 0 = the live required set equals the declared set and the pull-request declaration holds. 2 = a gate verdict: a declared context is not required (`gate-liveness: DENY - declared merge-blocking context(s) not required on <branch>: a, b`), or a context is required that the file does not declare (`gate-liveness: DENY - context(s) required on <branch> but not declared in docs/ci/required-gates.json: x`; a required context no job emits wedges every pull request), or the pull-request declaration is unmet. An empty rules array is a readable answer and is exit 2 with every declared context missing (this is also what a mistyped branch produces). 1 = the verdict could not be computed, never 0: `gh` missing, timed out or non-zero; empty, non-JSON or non-array output; a `required_status_checks` rule whose `parameters.required_status_checks` is not an array; an unreadable or invalid required-gates.json (unknown `pullRequestReview`, a blocking job without a non-empty `contexts` array, a non-blocking job without a non-empty `why`, a duplicate context, or no blocking context at all). Message: `gate-liveness: cannot verify the ruleset (<reason>) - failing closed`. Every DENY ends with the line `The ruleset is changed by a repository admin, never by this tool: see docs/ci/required-gates.md`. `--json` prints `{ ok, branch, declared, required, missing, undeclared, review }` on stdout for exit 0 and 2, and nothing on stdout for exit 1.
4. `pullRequestReview` is one of `none`, `code-owner` (`require_code_owner_review === true`), `approving` (`required_approving_review_count >= 1`), `either`; any `pull_request` rule in the array may satisfy it. The committed value is `none`: the repository has one collaborator, who authors the pull requests and cannot approve their own (docs/github-rulesets/README.md records the same reasoning for the count of 0). With `none` nothing is asserted and every run prints `gate-liveness: note - pull-request approval is declared "none"; not asserted`. Changing the policy later is a one-word edit to the JSON.
5. `.github/workflows/gate-liveness.yml`: triggers `push` to main, a daily `schedule`, and `workflow_dispatch`; NOT `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` (a pull request cannot repair a ruleset, so a PR-level red would block contributors on something none of them can fix). `permissions: contents: read`; checkout pinned to `ref: main` with `persist-credentials: false`; Node 20; no install step; one step `node scripts/gate-liveness.mjs --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`; no `continue-on-error`; action SHAs copied from ceremony-drift.yml. This run is EXPECTED to be red (exit 2, naming `rails-guard, mutation-gate, gate`) from the merge of this change until the owner updates the ruleset; say so in the PR description.
6. Keep the committed ruleset in step. In `docs/github-rulesets/main-branch-ruleset.json` replace ONLY the `required_status_checks` array with the six declared contexts in `--contexts` order, each as `{ "context": "...", "integration_id": 15368 }`; change nothing else in that file. In `docs/github-rulesets/README.md` update the `required_status_checks` table row to name the six contexts and add one sentence saying the list is declared in docs/ci/required-gates.json, that a test keeps the two files equal, and that scripts/gate-liveness.mjs compares the live ruleset with it.
7. Stale claims, comment-only edits. `.github/workflows/cross-model-gate.yml:25-31` (says the repo has no protection and the gate is only a signal), the ACTION REQUIRED banner at `.github/workflows/actionlint.yml:10-16`, and in `.github/workflows/router-drift.yml` the words "the permanent, required gate" at `:5` plus the whole banner at `:16-23` including the parenthetical that begins `(premortem`. Replace each with wording that is true before and after the ruleset changes: whether the job is declared merge-blocking is recorded in docs/ci/required-gates.json, and scripts/gate-liveness.mjs checks the live ruleset against it. Change no `on:`, `permissions:`, `concurrency:`, `jobs:` or step line in those three files.
8. `docs/ci/required-gates.md` (new, short): what the JSON is; how to add or retire a gate or a pull-request workflow (edit the JSON and, for a blocking context, main-branch-ruleset.json in the same change; the test forces the workflows and both files to move together; then an admin updates the ruleset); that the tool never writes to GitHub; the admin procedure (build the PUT body from the LIVE ruleset with `jq`, replacing only `required_status_checks` with `node scripts/gate-liveness.mjs --contexts`, each pinned to `integration_id` 15368 = GitHub Actions; `gh api -X PUT repos/voodootikigod/adlc/rulesets/17662766 --input <file>`; verify with `node scripts/gate-liveness.mjs` exiting 0; `docs/github-rulesets/apply.sh` now applies the same six contexts); and what an admin must know once `rails-guard` is required: a pull request that changes an immutable trust root keeps `rails-guard` red in a one-collaborator repository and merges only through the admin bypass; a direct push to main that adds a manifest segment turns `rails-guard` red on every open pull request until its branch is updated; a pull request from a fork that touches a trust root needs the `trust-root-change` label applied BEFORE its last push (the job reads labels from the event payload), an approving owner submission, and a re-run of the job, again after every push.
9. Regression guard: no existing file changes other than the three workflow comment blocks in item 7 and the two files in item 6. `packages/autopilot/lib/ci.mjs` `BLOCKING_PREFIXES` is a second, spec-defined list of blocking checks; do not edit it, assert agreement with it (AC8).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 Exit 2 when a declared context is absent: with today's live payload (only the three `test` contexts required) `main()` returns 2 and stderr names `rails-guard`, `mutation-gate` and `gate`. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`
- AC2 Fails closed, exit 1 and never 0, for each unverifiable input listed in NORMATIVE 3 and for an invalid `--repo` or `--branch`, with nothing on stdout under `--json`. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`
- AC3 Exit 0 when the live set equals the declared set; exit 2 when the ruleset requires a context the file does not declare; an empty rules array is exit 2. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`
- AC4 Pull-request modes: `none` asserts nothing and prints the note; `code-owner`, `approving` and `either` each return 2 when unmet and 0 when met. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`
- AC5 Bijectivity, both directions, with the failure message naming the offender: the set of workflow files under `.github/workflows/` that have a `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` trigger equals the set of workflow paths in the JSON; for every named workflow the job ids in the YAML equal the declared job ids; a blocking non-matrix job declares exactly `[<job id>]`; a blocking job with one matrix axis written as a flow sequence declares `<job id> (<value>)` per value; a blocking job with a job-level `name:` or a second matrix axis fails the test rather than guessing. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`
- AC6 The committed declaration enumerates the gates, and the real CLI prints them. The test spawns `process.execPath scripts/gate-liveness.mjs --contexts` and `--help` with a timeout and asserts stdout and exit 0. verify: `node -e "const g=require('./docs/ci/required-gates.json'); process.exit(['rails-guard','mutation-gate','cross-model-gate'].every(x=>JSON.stringify(g).includes(x))?0:1)"` exits 0, and `node scripts/gate-liveness.mjs --contexts` prints exactly `["test (18)","test (20)","test (22)","rails-guard","mutation-gate","gate"]`
- AC7 Read-only by construction: across every test the injected `runGh` receives `api` as its first argument, one `repos/.../rules/branches/...` path, and no `-X`, `--method`, `-f`, `-F` or `--input`; `defaultRunGh` with an injected `spawn` is shown to call `gh` with exactly the args it was given and `timeout: 30000`, and to map a spawn error, a signal and a non-zero status to `ok: false`. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`
- AC8 Consumer agreement: every declared blocking context is classified blocking by `blockingPrefixOf` from packages/autopilot/lib/ci.mjs (for `gate`, with the row's `workflow` set to the `name:` read from cross-model-gate.yml). verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs` and `node --test packages/autopilot/test/ci.test.mjs`
- AC9 Workflow wiring: gate-liveness.yml has the three triggers and neither pull-request trigger, runs `node scripts/gate-liveness.mjs`, has no `continue-on-error`, and the script imports only `node:` specifiers. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`
- AC10 Stale claims gone. verify: `! grep -nE "ACTION REQUIRED|Until that protection is configured|permanent, required gate|[(]premortem" .github/workflows/actionlint.yml .github/workflows/router-drift.yml .github/workflows/cross-model-gate.yml` exits 0 and prints nothing, and `test "$(grep -l "docs/ci/required-gates.json" .github/workflows/actionlint.yml .github/workflows/router-drift.yml .github/workflows/cross-model-gate.yml | wc -l)" -eq 3` exits 0
- AC11 Only comment lines changed in the three workflows, and the existing pins still pass. verify: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- .github/workflows/actionlint.yml .github/workflows/router-drift.yml .github/workflows/cross-model-gate.yml | grep -E "^[+-]" | grep -vE "^(\+\+\+|---) " | grep -vE "^[+-]#"` prints nothing, and `node --test packages/prosecute/test/cross-model-gate-workflow.test.mjs scripts/test/router-drift.test.mjs` passes
- AC12 docs/ci/required-gates.md carries the admin procedure. verify: `for p in "rulesets/17662766" "--contexts" "integration_id" "admin bypass" "trust-root-change"; do grep -q -e "$p" docs/ci/required-gates.md || exit 1; done` exits 0
- AC13 The committed ruleset agrees with the declaration: `evaluate({ gates, rules: <main-branch-ruleset.json>.rules }).ok` is true and every required entry carries `integration_id` 15368. verify: `node --test scripts/test/gate-liveness.test.mjs`, and `node -e "const r=require('./docs/github-rulesets/main-branch-ruleset.json').rules.find(x=>x.type==='required_status_checks').parameters.required_status_checks; process.exit(r.length===6&&r.every(c=>c.integration_id===15368)?0:1)"` exits 0, and `grep -q "required-gates.json" docs/github-rulesets/README.md` exits 0
- AC14 The comment gate passes on the branch. verify: `node scripts/check-reviewer-directed-comments.mjs origin/main` exits 0
- AC15 Guard (passes before and after): the change is not trust-root tier and touches nothing frozen. verify: `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --base origin/main` prints `NOT trust-root tier` and exits 0, and `node scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs origin/main` exits 0
- AC16 The scripts segment is green. verify: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs scripts`
- AC17 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally)

OUT OF SCOPE: changing any gate's internal logic; the human-gate binding (separate ticket); the ruleset edit itself (an admin action after merge); running or editing docs/github-rulesets/apply.sh; every edit to a frozen trust root, which belongs to one separate trust-root-change pull request: removing the `pre-ga-gate` job and its banner (.github/workflows/ci.yml:218-284) together with its `pre-ga-gate` entry here and the ADR 0003 note, the "private free-plan repo ... 403" rationale at ci.yml:80-90, the `/.adlc/tickets.json` entry at CODEOWNERS:42-44 and the "REQUIRES: branch protection must require CODEOWNERS review" claim at CODEOWNERS:65-69; adding gate-liveness to scripts/preflight.mjs or a package.json script; deleting router-drift.yml; renaming the `gate` job; making the in-session rails hook enforce rails inside `.worktrees/`.

allow-suppression: none
title: Make ADLC gates merge-blocking: declare the required checks + a gate-liveness meta-gate
